domain_context: Pure admission of one mechanically constructed candidate authorization command from complete server-owned resolver outputs before downstream authorization. Resolver lists preserve multiplicity.
rule: For a representable, fully supplied CommandBoundaryContext evaluated normally, return READY if and only if the inbound request_id is nonempty; exactly one authentication list entry has evidence_ref equal to the requested authentication_evidence_ref, nonempty evidence_ref and session_id, and trusted true; exactly one route list entry has route_id equal to the requested route_id, nonempty route_id and scope_evidence_ref, complete true, and nonempty required_permission resource, action and scope; and the candidate request_id equals the inbound request_id while its session_id, required_permission resource, action and scope, and scope_evidence_ref equal the values of those same unique qualifying rows. Exactly one counts list entries, including equal duplicates. Every other normally evaluated in-scope context returns DENY without a downstream authorization call.
applies_when: one fully supplied CommandBoundaryContext contains complete authentication and route-binding resolver lists preserving multiplicity and a candidate command
the selected typed Rules and command-boundary Operation evaluate normally
actors: trusted application constructing the candidate command and resolver context
outcomes: READY exactly when nonempty request identity, both unique qualifying rows, and exact same-row candidate provenance hold
DENY without downstream authorization call in every other normally evaluated in-scope context

examples.given: A nonempty request ID, exactly one fully qualifying authentication row and one fully qualifying route row, with candidate fields copied exactly from the request and those rows.
examples.when: The boundary evaluates the complete context.
examples.why: Every qualifier and same-row provenance condition holds.

examples.given: Both resolver lists each contain exactly one qualifying row and the candidate matches every source, but request and candidate request IDs are empty.
examples.when: The boundary evaluates the complete context.
examples.then: DENY is returned without downstream authorization.
examples.why: The inbound request identity is empty.

counterexamples.given: An otherwise valid context has empty request and candidate request IDs.
counterexamples.why: READY requires nonempty inbound request identity.

counterexamples.given: A unique qualifying authentication row has session S1, while a second matching but nonqualifying row has an empty session.
counterexamples.when: The candidate takes its session from the nonqualifying row and an implementation returns READY.
counterexamples.why: Provenance must use the same unique qualifying row.

counterexamples.given: Two equal qualifying entries occur in either resolver list.
counterexamples.when: An implementation collapses them and returns READY.
counterexamples.why: Exactly-one counts list entries, not distinct values.

counterexamples.given: A matching route row is complete but has an empty required_permission.action.
counterexamples.when: An implementation treats it as qualifying and returns READY.
counterexamples.why: All three permission components must be nonempty.

counterexamples.given: Every READY condition holds in a normally evaluated context.
counterexamples.why: The positive READY branch is required.

boundaries: This draft concerns the command-boundary READY/DENY decision, not downstream authorization ALLOW/DENY.
No behavior is asserted for exceptions, nontermination, missing resolver outputs, or contexts outside the selected typed contract.
The predecessor draft and its historical v1 contradiction remain pinned evidence; this candidate does not retroactively repair or accept them.
Finite native witnesses and source-bound AST identity do not prove all-context preservation.
No production authentication, authorization, security, EVF pass, F5 satisfaction, or runtime_guarantees_observed is asserted.

formal.definition: One fully supplied typed request, complete finite ordered authentication and route resolver lists, and one candidate authorization command.
formal.expression: Context = (Request, List AuthEvidence, List RouteBinding, CandidateCommand); lists preserve positions and multiplicity
formal.operational_interpretation: Evaluate the selected typed context without deduplicating, dropping, or supplementing resolver rows.

definitions.plain_language: The whole input to one boundary decision, including every resolver row in order.
forbidden_collapses: partial context treated as a complete evaluation
list converted to a set

formal.definition: The fixed input-domain condition for the accepted normally evaluated rule, independent of the observed outcome; the Context carrier is already limited to complete representable finite-list inputs.

notation.meaning: Every c in the fixed Context carrier is in scope.

formal.operational_interpretation: Determine the Context carrier from the input contract before evaluation; establish selected evaluator normal completion by a separate correspondence proof, never by filtering out an incorrect result.

definitions.plain_language: The rule applies to complete inputs the selected evaluator can normally evaluate.
definitions.domain_context: Exceptions, missing outputs and nontermination remain outside the claim, not silent failures counted as DENY.
forbidden_collapses: post-hoc scope narrowing after a wrong result
missing resolver output treated as an empty complete list

formal.definition: One authentication resolver entry identified by its context and zero-based position, not by its row value.
formal.expression: AuthOccurrence(c,i) iff 0 ≤ i < length(c.authRows); (c,i)=(c,j) iff i=j; nonmember ghosts keep the global sort nonempty

notation.meaning: Authentication entry at position i of c's list.

formal.operational_interpretation: Equal rows at two list positions remain two occurrences; field projections are total but ghosts and foreign positions are never members.

definitions.plain_language: Count entries, even if two entries contain identical data.
definitions.domain_context: Authentication resolver list ambiguity must not disappear through deduplication.
forbidden_collapses: row-value equality used as occurrence identity
ghost occurrence qualifying as a list entry

formal.definition: One route resolver entry identified by its context and zero-based position, not by its row value.
formal.expression: RouteOccurrence(c,j) iff 0 ≤ j < length(c.routeRows); (c,j)=(c,k) iff j=k; nonmember ghosts keep the global sort nonempty

notation.meaning: Route entry at position j of c's list.

formal.operational_interpretation: Equal rows at two list positions remain two occurrences; field projections are total but ghosts and foreign positions are never members.

definitions.plain_language: Count every route entry, including equal duplicates.
definitions.domain_context: Route resolver list ambiguity must not disappear through deduplication.
forbidden_collapses: row-value equality used as occurrence identity
ghost occurrence qualifying as a list entry

formal.definition: A member authentication occurrence meeting every accepted evidence-reference, trust and session qualifier.
formal.expression: QA(c,a) := AuthMember(c,a) ∧ EvidenceRef(a)=RequestedEvidenceRef(c) ∧ EvidenceRef(a)≠empty ∧ SessionID(a)≠empty ∧ Trusted(a)=true

notation.meaning: a is one fully qualifying authentication list position for c.

formal.operational_interpretation: Check all four field conditions on the same resolver entry after membership; do not use a weaker matching row for provenance.

definitions.plain_language: A trusted matching auth row with real evidence and session IDs.
definitions.domain_context: One such list entry is necessary, and two equal qualifying entries are ambiguous.
forbidden_collapses: matching evidence reference alone treated as qualification
nonqualifying row used for candidate session provenance

formal.definition: A member route occurrence meeting every accepted route, completeness, scope-evidence and permission-component qualifier.
formal.expression: QR(c,r) := RouteMember(c,r) ∧ RouteID(r)=RequestedRouteID(c) ∧ RouteID(r)≠empty ∧ ScopeEvidenceRef(r)≠empty ∧ Complete(r)=true ∧ PermissionResource(r)≠empty ∧ PermissionAction(r)≠empty ∧ PermissionScope(r)≠empty

notation.meaning: r is one fully qualifying route list position for c.

formal.operational_interpretation: Check all seven field conditions on the same route entry after membership; no missing permission component can qualify.

definitions.plain_language: A complete matching route row with real scope evidence and all three permission fields.
definitions.domain_context: One such list entry is necessary, and two equal qualifying entries are ambiguous.
forbidden_collapses: complete route treated as qualified despite empty permission component
matching route ID alone treated as qualification

formal.definition: Existence and uniqueness over qualifying list positions within one context.
formal.expression: ExactOneAuth(c,a) := QA(c,a) ∧ ∀a2:AuthOccurrence.(QA(c,a2) ⇒ a2=a); ExactOneRoute(c,r) := QR(c,r) ∧ ∀r2:RouteOccurrence.(QR(c,r2) ⇒ r2=r)

notation.meaning: a and r are their respective unique fully qualifying list positions.

formal.operational_interpretation: Count list entries, not distinct row values; retain the unique witnesses for provenance checks.

definitions.plain_language: There is one and only one qualifying entry in each list.
definitions.domain_context: Equal duplicate entries make exactly-one false.
forbidden_collapses: uniqueness over row values instead of list positions
existence without uniqueness

formal.definition: Candidate request fields equal the inbound request and the same unique qualifying authentication and route occurrences supply every candidate field.

notation.meaning: Candidate fields copied from the request and the already bound unique a and r.

formal.operational_interpretation: Use the a and r that satisfy ExactOneAuth and ExactOneRoute; do not search again over weaker or different resolver rows.

definitions.plain_language: Copy candidate values from the exact rows that passed the uniqueness checks.
definitions.domain_context: A different matching but nonqualifying row cannot supply a candidate field.
forbidden_collapses: candidate provenance from an independently chosen row
permission triple partially copied from different route rows

formal.definition: The complete positive branch of the accepted command-boundary biconditional, with unique occurrence witnesses scoped over provenance.

notation.meaning: All owner-accepted READY conditions hold in c.

formal.operational_interpretation: Return READY exactly when this predicate holds; both absence and excess of qualifying entries make it false.

definitions.plain_language: A real request ID, one qualifying row of each kind, and a candidate copied from those rows.
definitions.domain_context: The command-boundary decision is pure and precedes downstream authorization.
forbidden_collapses: always DENY despite a valid context
blank inbound request ID treated as READY

formal.definition: One abstract pure command-boundary outcome in the distinct exhaustive set {READY,DENY}, tied to ReadyCondition by both biconditionals on every in-scope normal context.

notation.meaning: Abstract command-boundary outcome before downstream authorization.

formal.operational_interpretation: Compare the selected typed Operation result to this abstract decision only through a separate exact source/preservation binding.

definitions.plain_language: READY exactly for valid contexts, otherwise DENY; never confuse it with the downstream decision.
definitions.domain_context: A downstream DENY after READY does not mean the command boundary denied or skipped the call.
forbidden_collapses: kernel DENY confused with downstream DENY
one-way implication replacing biconditional
